source: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 1 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 1
knowledgePattern: Compare the full one-root parameter range with sufficient subsets
solution:
Put f(x)=x3−3px2+4. Then f′(x)=3x(x−2p), so for p≠0 the stationary inputs are 0 and 2p, with heights 4 and 4−4p3.

If p<1, both heights are positive. The cubic has one crossing on its leftmost increasing branch and no others; this also covers p<0, when the order of the stationary inputs reverses. If p=0, f(x)=x3+4 is strictly increasing and has one root.

At p=1, f(x)=(x−2)2(x+1) has two distinct real roots. For p>1, the maximum is positive and minimum negative, giving three distinct roots. Thus the full one-root condition is p<1.

The condition |p|<1 guarantees this but excludes successful values such as p=−2, so it is sufficient but not necessary. Each other proposed condition permits p=1 or some p>1. Answer E.

hints.title: Locate the turning heights
hints.body: Differentiate with respect to x, treating p as fixed. Evaluate the original cubic at each stationary input.
hints.recap: Stationary inputs come from the derivative; their heights come from the original function.
hints.pitfall: Check separately if the stationary inputs coincide.
hints.pause: Find the stationary inputs and their heights.

recall.reminder: Stationary inputs come from the derivative; their heights come from the original function.

hints.title: Count before comparing the options
hints.body: Use the signs of the turning heights and the cubic tails to find the complete parameter set giving exactly one distinct root.
hints.recap: A touching root counts once when distinct real roots are counted.
hints.pitfall: A horizontal tangent on the axis is still a root.
hints.pause: Check the boundary values as well as the open parameter intervals.

recall.reminder: A touching root counts once when distinct real roots are counted.

hints.title: Test the direction of the condition
hints.body: Compare each option with your full successful set: a sufficient condition must lie wholly inside it, while necessity would require every successful value.
hints.recap: A proper subset of a successful parameter set can be sufficient without being necessary.
hints.pitfall: Do not require a sufficient condition to describe every successful parameter.
hints.pause: Select the condition and give a successful value it excludes.

recall.reminder: A proper subset of a successful parameter set can be sufficient without being necessary.
